title: Level 5 (World Class) - C-12
notes:
West leads the ♠3 against 7♠. If it were not for West's excellent trump lead, 13 tricks would be easy on a crossruff. After winning the first trick South should try to establish dummy's hearts by ruffing out the suit. West's discard on the second round of hearts complicates matters.

West has shown at least 5-5 in the minors with his unusual notrump overcall. South must hope that West began with 2155 distribution including the ♣K and ♣Q. South should crossruff the next several tricks, making sure to keep the ♣J and a small diamond in the closed hand.

When South ruffs a heart with his last trump, a heart trick will be established in the dummy, but West's remaining trump appears as if it will be a problem. In fact, West will be caught in a rare backwash squeeze on this trick.

If West underruffs, the rest will be easy as the dummy will be high. If, instead, West discards from either minor, South's last card in that suit will become a winner and the lead of that card will act as a trump substitute and allow declarer to win the last 2 tricks.

There are several types of backwash squeezes, all of which are characterized by a defender being squeezed in 3 suits, including the trump suit. The backwash squeeze gets its name from its unusual property that the suits that West guards are all sitting over the threat cards in the South hand. This form of backwash squeeze does not gain a trick in its own right, but instead allows declarer to compensate for a shortage of entries required to complete a suit establishment.
